attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post, asserted in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithfully lists the four output categories. 'Already' means these outputs have happened, not that they are typical.

contract.note: The plain reading is that these outputs have occurred, with no frequency claim. That is the ordinary reading of 'already'. The contract discloses the API-versus-consumer-app caveat for the code study.

evidence.note: March 2024 audit: ChatGPT 3.5 gave false voting procedures for EU elections. The audit also says most answers were acceptable.
April 2023 firsthand report of ChatGPT giving explosives instructions after a jailbreak. Whether the instructions would work was not tested.
Peer-reviewed study (data from Feb 2023): one ChatGPT response sent a patient with crushing chest pain to a community clinic as an option. That is clinically risky advice.
Preprint finds 248 CWE vulnerabilities in code from gpt-3.5-turbo, accessed through the API rather than the consumer app.

reviews.rationale: Dated records from before 2024-07-16 show ChatGPT outputs in all four categories: false election information, bomb instructions under a jailbreak, risky chest-pain advice, and vulnerable code. The counterevidence shows most outputs were acceptable, but the claim only asserts that these outputs occurred.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: An unqualified, open-ended forecast that the LLM will not destroy society, combined with a present-tense claim about OpenAI's research direction. The contract scores only the forecast part.

contract.note: Fair. A forecast with no deadline cannot be confirmed by any finite period without the event. It can only be contradicted by a documented catastrophe.

evidence.note: 2026 safety report: current systems fall short of loss-of-control capability. It neither documents societal destruction nor rules it out.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. No conclusive event (societal destruction caused by an OpenAI LLM) is documented, and under the contract, time passing without such an event cannot support the claim. It stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense claim that LLMs as of July 2024 lacked the capabilities needed for OpenAI's level 2. The proposition matches it.

contract.note: Defining 'reasoner' as PhD-level problem solving without tools follows the contemporaneous reporting and is a fair reading. The result depends on that definition, and no test with a pass threshold exists.

evidence.note: Reports OpenAI's own self-classification as on the cusp of level 2. This is a company disclosure about OpenAI only, not an independent evaluation of all LLMs.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is OpenAI's self-reported status, relayed through the press. There is no contemporaneous broad evaluation against a level-2 standard. 'Not yet attained' is weaker than 'incapable', and other labs' models are not covered. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: A largely evaluative description of the Bloomberg and Reuters stories. The proposition preserves it, though 'marketing collateral' and 'hollow' are metaphorical.

contract.note: The plain reading (the stories promote unverified claims rather than show a demonstrated advance) is ordinary and fair. The result depends on how 'breakthrough' and 'hollow' are read, and the speaker set no threshold for either.

evidence.note: Bloomberg describes the levels as a work in progress, which supports the point that this was not a breakthrough. It also reports an internal demo whose substance is unknown.
Reuters reports claimed demos and an internal MATH score above 90%, but could not link them to Strawberry. This complicates 'hollow' without validating any breakthrough.

reviews.rationale: The articles show the levels framework was provisional, and the Strawberry claims were unverified at the time. They also report internal demos and benchmark results that no one could check. Whether the underlying work was hollow, or whether the pieces were promotional in intent, cannot be settled from the packet.
